ai-at-work.title: What happens when companies become too AI-pilled?
ai-at-work.excerpt: The people deciding that AI can replace your job are also the ones least likely to understand what your job truly involves, according to Box founder Aaron Levie, who pointed to this as an example of “
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are rushing to replace workers with AI without understanding what those workers actually do, a phenomenon Box founder Aaron Levie calls "AI psychosis." This matters because digital workplace leaders are caught between board pressure to automate everything and the reality that most job elimination decisions are made by people who've never done the work being eliminated. The irony is that the executives most confidently slashing headcount are probably the same ones who'll panic when critical institutional knowledge walks out the door with the people they fired.

ai-at-work.title: Final 24 hours to save up to $410 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket
ai-at-work.excerpt: You now have until tonight at 11:59 p.m. PT to lock in Early Bird savings of up to $410 for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 before prices increase. Join 10,000+ tech leaders in October for one of the most ant
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch is running a last-chance promotion for early bird discounts on Disrupt 2026 tickets, offering up to $410 off before prices jump tonight. If you're a digital workplace leader looking to stay current on enterprise tech trends and network with peers in the space, this is worth considering. That said, before you drop four hundred bucks, ask yourself honestly whether you'll actually attend or if you'll just end up with another conference t-shirt gathering dust in your closet.

ai-at-work.title: Glean’s top line crosses $300M as AI budget cutting becomes its major selling point
ai-at-work.excerpt: The enterprise AI search startup tripled its annual revenue even as tech giants entered the category.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Glean, an enterprise AI search platform, hit $300M in annual revenue while competitors like Microsoft and Google moved into the same space. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because it shows that specialized AI search built specifically for work context is winning against general-purpose tools shoehorned into enterprise. The real story isn't that Glean is selling AI, it's that companies are desperate enough to cut through information overload that they'll pay premium prices for something that actually works instead of settling for whatever their software vendor bundles in.

ai-at-work.title: The internet is being rebuilt for machines
ai-at-work.excerpt: As AI agents move from experiments to production, AWS, Cloudflare, and others are redesigning cloud infrastructure for a future dominated by machine-generated internet traffic instead of human users.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Cloud giants are restructuring their entire infrastructure because AI agents will soon generate way more traffic than people do. This matters because your digital workplace tech stack will live on infrastructure optimized for machine-to-machine communication, which fundamentally changes how apps perform, scale, and cost money. The funny part is we spent thirty years building the internet for humans, and now we're basically starting over because our robots are chattier than we are.

tools-tech.title: After using this Windows laptop for work and play, I'm wondering why I still need my PC tower
tools-tech.excerpt: The MSI Raider 16 Max HX combines powerful current-gen hardware with a revamped cooling system and a stunning 240Hz OLED screen.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Someone tested a high-end gaming laptop for mixed work and personal use and found it handled everything without needing a separate desktop tower. This matters because it reflects a real shift in how knowledge workers actually use devices, which means IT leaders need to rethink their one-device-per-worker mentality and support strategies. Here's the thing though: just because a laptop can do it all doesn't mean your organization's security policies, VPN throughput, or thermal management actually want it to.

tools-tech.title: Open-source security is a mess - IBM and Red Hat bet $5 billion and 20,000 engineers can fix it
tools-tech.excerpt: Project Lightwell is an AI‑powered initiative to find and fix vulnerabilities in open-source software at an industrial scale. Here's what we know so far.
tools-tech.dwp_take: IBM and Red Hat are dumping $5 billion and 20,000 engineers into Project Lightwell, an AI system designed to scan open-source code for vulnerabilities at scale. This matters because your entire tech stack probably runs on open-source libraries that nobody's properly maintaining, which means your security posture is essentially a game of Russian roulette. Look, I'll believe it when I see it, but at least someone's finally admitting that open-source security is held together with duct tape and good intentions.

tools-tech.title: Open source Euro-Office productivity suite to launch June 9
tools-tech.excerpt: The Euro-Office open source productivity app suite will be available with the first stable release of the software on June 9. Euro-Office was unveiled in March with the aim of providing a modern, open
tools-tech.dwp_take: A European open source productivity suite called Euro-Office is launching June 9 with four browser-based apps designed to compete with Microsoft and Google offerings. This matters because it gives digital workplace leaders an actual alternative for organizations that genuinely need to reduce dependence on US tech vendors, which is becoming a real compliance and political issue in Europe. The timing is interesting, but let's be honest: open source productivity suites have a graveyard behind them, so this one will live or die based on whether it actually works smoothly and whether IT teams will support it.

tools-tech.title: Meta considers becoming a hyperscaler
tools-tech.excerpt: Meta has raised the possibility that it could be joining the likes of Amazon, Microsoft and Google in offering cloud services at some point in the future — although potential customers shouldn’t be ad
tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta is exploring the idea of entering the cloud services market as a hyperscaler, potentially competing with Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, though nothing concrete has been announced yet. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because it could eventually expand your options for infrastructure providers and potentially shift pricing dynamics in an already competitive market. Honestly, Meta entering the hyperscaler game feels like watching someone casually mention they might learn to juggle while their house is on fire, but stranger things have happened in tech.

digital-culture.title: To stay active or to step away: Older Americans face a double standard in the workplace
digital-culture.excerpt: There is a scene in The Devil Wears Prada 2 where legendary fashion editor Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, is walking alone through Milan’s fashion district. Her influence has been built on
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new Fast Company piece uses Miranda Priestly's struggle with relevance in fashion to spotlight how older workers face impossible choices: stay visible and risk being seen as clinging to power, or step back and risk being forgotten. This matters because digital workplace leaders are actively designing the tools, communication channels, and culture that either amplify or silence different age groups, often without realizing it. Here's the thing though: if your digital workplace strategy requires people to choose between staying relevant and staying sane, you've built a broken system, not a modern one.

digital-culture.title: Why the hardest skills in leadership are the ones we’ve typically called soft
digital-culture.excerpt: In the late 1960s, the U.S. Army made a distinction between the skills necessary for machinery operations and those used in service of people management. Hard skills, as the Army framed it, were the c
digital-culture.dwp_take: The Army's decades-old distinction between hard skills (operating equipment) and soft skills (managing people) is finally being recognized as backwards, since leadership competencies like communication and emotional intelligence are genuinely difficult to master. This matters to digital workplace pros because we spend enormous energy building systems and infrastructure when the real bottleneck in most organizations is actually leadership quality, not technology. Here's the thing: calling them "soft" skills was always corporate gaslighting that let incompetent managers off the hook, so maybe we stop pretending that actually knowing how to lead people is somehow easier than learning software.

digital-culture.title: Congrats on that promotion. Are you sure you want it?
digital-culture.excerpt: “I wish I had slowed down to reflect more deeply on this opportunity before saying yes.” That’s what Tanya told me in a coaching session. Even though she had just been promoted, she was close to burno
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece chronicles how Tanya rushed into a director promotion at her consulting firm, only to find herself burned out within months because she didn't properly evaluate whether the role actually suited her. This matters to digital workplace folks because promotion fever often hits right when you're doing well in your current role, and nobody stops to ask whether the new gig will destroy your life or just change it. Here's the thing: if you're excited enough about a promotion to say yes in the first meeting, you probably weren't thinking clearly enough to say no, and that's exactly when you should have paused.

digital-culture.title: How to hack your calendar for more vacation by ‘PTO-maxxing’
digital-culture.excerpt: Paid time off is precious. The average private-sector worker in the U.S. who has been at their job for at least a year is given 11 days of paid leave annually, according to the Bureau of Labor Statist
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new trend called "PTO-maxxing" is getting attention as a way for workers to stretch their limited vacation time more effectively. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that burnout prevention isn't just about wellness messaging; it's about employees actually disconnecting, and that's hard when people only get 11 days off annually. Here's the thing though: no calendar hack fixes the real problem, which is that American PTO is embarrassingly low compared to the rest of the developed world, so stop pretending productivity tools solve what policy should.

industry-news.title: BYD Offers Crash Cost Coverage for God’s Eye Assisted Driving
industry-news.excerpt: BYD says it will cover some God’s Eye crash costs, but drivers still need to know when the guarantee applies and where the limits are. The post BYD Offers Crash Cost Coverage for God’s Eye Assisted Dr
industry-news.dwp_take: BYD is offering to cover some crash costs for vehicles using their God's Eye assisted driving system, though coverage comes with plenty of fine print about when it actually applies. This matters to digital workplace professionals because autonomous vehicle tech increasingly touches corporate fleet management and employee safety policies, forcing IT leaders to understand liability and insurance implications. Here's the thing: offering crash coverage while hiding the real limits in the T's and C's is basically the automotive equivalent of "we've secured your data" in a breach notification letter, and we all know how that usually ends.

industry-news.title: Carnival Data Breach Exposes Data of Nearly 6 Million Customers
industry-news.excerpt: Carnival says a data breach exposed personal information of nearly 6 million customers after a social engineering attack tied to a single employee account. The post Carnival Data Breach Exposes Data o
industry-news.dwp_take: A social engineering attack targeting one employee account at Carnival compromised personal data for nearly 6 million customers, proving once again that your strongest security system crumbles when someone clicks the wrong link. Digital workplace leaders need to understand that endpoint security and fancy firewalls mean nothing if your workforce doesn't know how to spot a phishing attempt, which is why security training needs to be actual training, not a checkbox. The irony here is brutal: one person's bad day just made millions of vacationers' days significantly worse.

industry-news.title: Samsung Rolls Out Passport Verification Feature Inside Wallet App
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung Wallet now supports CLEAR-verified digital IDs based on US passports for domestic travel at more than 250 TSA checkpoints. The post Samsung Rolls Out Passport Verification Feature Inside Walle
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung has added digital ID verification to its Wallet app, letting travelers use their phones instead of physical passports at TSA checkpoints across the country. This matters to digital workplace professionals because mobile identity verification will eventually replace passwords and physical credentials in corporate environments, so understanding how it works in travel scenarios teaches you what's coming to your office. Honestly, if TSA can verify your identity from your phone, your IT department has zero excuses left for making employees remember sixteen different passwords.

industry-news.title: Leaked Disney Document Points to Hulu App Shutdown After Disney+ Transition
industry-news.excerpt: A leaked internal Disney document points to a possible shutdown of the standalone Hulu app after users move to Disney+. For media and technology teams, the shift highlights the complexity of consolida
industry-news.dwp_take: Disney is apparently planning to shut down the standalone Hulu app and fold everything into Disney+, which means migrating millions of user accounts, preferences, and billing systems in one go. This matters to digital workplace professionals because it's a textbook example of the nightmare scenarios that keep integration projects awake at night: consolidating apps, profiles, recommendations, and ad systems across a global platform is exponentially harder than it sounds on a PowerPoint slide. If even Disney with unlimited resources is treating this cautiously enough to leak documents, imagine what happens when your mid-market company tries to consolidate two enterprise systems.
